The question is in Russian: "How is it customary to briefly denote the shooting and death of a group of members of the imperial family in a mine shaft in the Urals in the summer of 1918?"

This refers to the execution of the Romanov family. The specific event - the murder of members of the imperial family in a mine shaft in the Urals in summer 1918. Wait, actually the main Romanov family (Nicholas II and family) were shot in the basement of the Ipatiev House, not a mine shaft. But there was a group killed at a mine shaft - the "Alapaevsk" murders, where Grand Duchess Elizabeth Feodorovna and other Romanovs were thrown into a mine shaft near Alapayevsk.

The term for this in Russian history: "Алапаевские мученики" (Alapaevsk martyrs) or "Алапаевское убийство" / "Алапаевская трагедия". The group is often called "Алапаевские мученики".
